rationale: The source carries two separable obligations with different activation and evidence. (1) Closed vocabulary: segment 5 must be one of the five core layers; this is mechanical, fired by the bun_green_traceability_detector finding, and proven by the detector. (2) Responsibility match: the chosen layer must reflect the file's real architectural responsibility; this needs a judgment about what the file actually does, carries the During-GREEN repair moves (derive from architecture, follow nearest pattern, move only the misplaced implementation) and the anti-relabelling bans, and is proven by showing that the URN layer matches the implementation's actual architectural layer, plus the passing acceptance. The source does not say who gives that proof. The source's canonical path ('declare one of the five ... according to the file's real responsibility') makes both jointly mandatory, so the parts require each other. The During-GREEN qualifier stays local to the responsibility part and no phase-loop shared node is used.

parts.given: A file declares a six-segment URN; segment 5 is the layer the boundary and dependency-flow rules read to judge imports.
parts.when: You write or change the URN, or the detector reports its layer as invalid.
parts.then: Set segment 5 to exactly one of `domain`, `application`, `integration`, `presentation`, `assembly`.
avoid: Inventing a new layer. Core fixes the vocabulary, not this extension; a new layer is a core change.
unless: The URN is not six segments; it is skipped.
parts.why: Layering rules read segment 5 to decide whether an import is legal. A layer outside the vocabulary is not just mislabelled: no layering rule can reach the file, so it becomes a hole that lets any dependency pass unchallenged.
evidence: bun_green_traceability_detector reports no GREEN-URN-006 / BUN-GREEN-URN-LAYER-001 finding.
verifier_detail: Check segment 5 of each URN against the closed set {domain, application, integration, presentation, assembly}.
Skip URNs that do not have exactly six segments.
Core owns the vocabulary, not the Bun extension; reject extension-local additions.
